<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fdeeea0cc9183f9c80343a552ef6523b1a53f99b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ba04e08eb6b835cb4b6b209f79509be6bd9247b5` — the merge of head `123df25c8cff643070d030f6b294a6745a864cc1` into base `fdeeea0cc9183f9c80343a552ef6523b1a53f99b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ba04e08eb6b835cb4b6b209f79509be6bd9247b5 && git checkout ba04e08eb6b835cb4b6b209f79509be6bd9247b5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fdeeea0cc9183f9c80343a552ef6523b1a53f99b 123df25c8cff643070d030f6b294a6745a864cc1 && git checkout -B drift-repro fdeeea0cc9183f9c80343a552ef6523b1a53f99b && git merge --no-ff 123df25c8cff643070d030f6b294a6745a864cc1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fdeeea0cc9183f9c80343a552ef6523b1a53f99b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e5f4958c03d8f0663c06bf646f52df722e2d6da2`

<sub>Reviewed and posted 2026-09-24T01:28Z by the at-tier review subagent the `domain:spec#5` seat spawned … (read: the diff, both commits, PR body, changeset, #19101 with comments `5787429974` / `5805027961` / `5805064236` / `5805539465`, #19930, zod 4.6.1 `to-json-schema.js` + `registries.js`, AGENTS.md, contract-review.md, the head's 46 check-runs · ran, in a detached worktree at the head with deps installed: the PR's test file (14/14), both ablations, 17 synthetic probes base-vs-head, and a leaf-by-leaf corpus diff over base/head × lazy/eager (eager entered through `src/index.ts`) · NOT MEASURED: `/meta/types` and `os generate` through the real `protocol.ts` / CLI binaries (need the built consumer closure; their conversion calls were replicated verbatim instead), an eager `gen:openapi` run (crashes on #19930), the dev's unfiled tsx env-hoisting note)</sub>

### ① Derived judgments

**Bytes (base→head, lazy; own harness, 1125 leaves added, 0 removed, 0 changed, every one a `description`):** `openapi.json` nine +2 (`ListRecordResponse.properties.data.items`, `BulkRequest.properties.records.items`, both "Key-value map of record data") — matches the PR. `os generate` ladder (tier 3, input/any) +445 — matches. approval-node +0, schemaless +0 — matches. `/meta/types` through the served conversion (`toJsonSchemaSafe` replicated: `override: markErasedAuthoringInput`, degenerate retry, `stripUnauthorableProperties`) **+183 across 12 of 26 types**, not 170/11: `action` +13 (`ActionSchema` is a pipe whose bare output conversion is a husk; the override re-derives it from the input side, and the 13 lazy `I18nLabel`/`options.label` leaves inside then carry their description). The bare `z.toJSONSchema(schema, { unrepresentable: 'any' })` the dev describes reproduces 170/11 exactly, so the dev measured a conversion the endpoint does not serve for `action`. Producers the PR does not enumerate also move, description-only: `driverConfigJsonSchema` (+9: sqlite, sqliteWasm, memory root descriptions and memory `persistence` branches — runtime-served as `DriverDefinitionSchema.configSchema`), `build-react-blocks-contract`'s per-block conversion (+29 nested leaves; `gen:react-blocks` re-run at head leaves `react-blocks.md` byte-unchanged), `reference-sites.ts`'s input-io conversion of the same 26 types (+287). **Lazy vs eager after the fix: 0 diffs on every corpus. Eager before vs after: byte-identical (3,209,739 B both).** Only `description` moves and only toward eager — confirmed.

**Registry semantics:** `ctx.metadataRegistry` is `params.metadata ?? z.globalRegistry` (zod `initializeContext`), so by default the alias is a write into the **global** registry, keyed on the Proxy, WeakMap-held, persisting past the conversion: `z.globalRegistry.has(proxy)` flips false→true after the first conversion and `get(proxy)` then answers the real's merged metadata less `id` (P1). Per-registry: a custom `metadata:` registry receives the alias and the global one is untouched (P2); a fresh registry without the real yields no description, the same as eager (P4). Never clobbers a caller's own entry on the Proxy (P3). Twice = same output (P4). Concurrency: `toJSONSchema` is synchronous, nothing interleaves. `.description` / `.meta()` reads through the Proxy resolve on the real and are unchanged before/after (P12); `_idmap` untouched (P13). One semantic the docblock's "once" implies but does not spell out: the alias is a snapshot — an in-place `globalRegistry.add(real, …)` after the first conversion is invisible to later lazy conversions while eager sees it (P5: lazy "v1", eager "v2"). No repo site does this (the only non-PR `globalRegistry.add` is on a fresh clone, `scripts/lib/dropped-refinements.ts:240`). Correction to the mechanism as written: base did not merely *lose* the description — `$ZodRegistry.get` merges the `_zod.parent` chain, which the Proxy shares, so base emitted the **ancestor's** metadata (P1 base: `description` from the `.describe()` parent, `title` from the own `.meta()` dropped; P11 base: "inherited" instead of "own"). Head fixes both and pins the parent case.

**`id` left un-aliased:** right. Every conversion through the Proxy enters both identities into `seen` (the facade's existing `seen.set(real, entry)`), and `extractDefs` compares keys, so an aliased `id` throws "Duplicate schema id" on any nested lazy reference — ablation confirmed (below). What an id-bearing lazy schema emits is a pre-existing structural divergence the PR neither worsens nor fixes: nested → `$defs.__schema0` instead of the named def (P6a, P6d); root → inline instead of `$ref`+named def (P6b); optional+`z.lazy` → one `$ref` to the named def (via the real) plus one inline copy (P6c). Head adds the description to that def/inline copy; base and head both `same:false` against eager. Corpus exposure: 0 — `grep '.meta({ … id:'` over non-test `packages/spec/src`: 0 hits.

**Pins (re-measured):** deleting `aliasMetadataOntoProxy(ctx?.metadataRegistry, real);` → 4 failed / 10 passed (the four new cases; "expected undefined to be 'Key-value map of record data'", "expected 'inherited' to be 'own'"). Deleting `delete aliased.id;` → 1 failed / 13 passed, "Duplicate schema id \"LazySchemaIdProbe19101\"". Coverage: nested array item ✓, root ✓, parent-inherited ✓, `id` exclusion ✓, real contract vs a true eager child ✓; a Proxy referenced twice is only half-asserted (the `id` pin checks `b`, not `a`); no pin for a described pipe/transform, self-recursion, other meta keys, or a custom registry. My probes read equal to eager on head for all of them (P7 pipe out/in/root, P8 recursion root/nested, P9 twice in both orders incl. `reused:'ref'`, P10, P17 lazy-of-lazy).

**Other metadata keys:** everything except `id` rides (`title`, `examples`, `deprecated`, custom keys — P10), which is what eager emits; correct.

**Shipped sentences:** docblock — "zod reads … `ctx.metadataRegistry.get(node)` right after this hook returns" ✓ (`processSchema` lines 93–116); "the registry merges a node's `_zod.parent` chain on read" ✓; "in the registry this conversion reads" is true but omits that this is the global registry by default; "lost its authored description" understates (ancestor metadata was emitted, above); "the OpenAPI artifact, `/meta/types` and the `os generate` IDE schema all shipped the lazy, description-less answer" — description-less for those nodes only. Changeset — "`GET …/openapi.json` document served from it" ✓ (`rest-server.ts:5134` reads the shipped file and spreads `components`); "gains 2 (…)" ✓; "170 across 11 of 26" ✗ (183/12 served); "the four affected surfaces" ✗ (at least seven producers move); "approval-node and schemaless … unchanged" ✓; "No other key differs … eager outputs are byte-identical" ✓; "every runtime producer runs lazily" — true by default for the set found (`protocol.ts`, `reference-sites.ts`, `erased-authoring-mark.ts`, `cli/generate.ts`, `approval.zod.ts`, `schemaless-node-config.zod.ts`, `driver/common.zod.ts`; none sets the flag). Test docblock — "every `/meta/types` schema 170" reads as per-schema and carries the wrong total. PR body — ablation counts ✓, "170 across 11 of 26" ✗. Model identifiers: swept diff, commits, body, changeset — none.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec` is right (bug fix in a released package) and matches the PR body. `Clause-②: no` holds: the 1125 moved leaves are all `description` (an annotation), no validation keyword, `$defs`, `$ref` or `required` moves in any corpus, and the parse path is untouched (the facade still prototype-delegates `_zod.run`; the alias runs only inside `processJSONSchema`).

### ③ Boundary flags

Blocking:
- **B1 — wrong count in shipped prose (changeset → CHANGELOG, test docblock, PR body): "`/meta/types` gain 170 across 11 of 26 types".** Measured through the served conversion: **183 across 12 of 26** (`action` +13; per type: action 13, agent 1, app 13, dashboard 13, dataset 5, object 16, page 17, report 14, seed 1, tool 1, translation 3, view 86). 170/11 reproduces only with a bare `unrepresentable:'any'` conversion, under which `action` is a husk `/meta/types` never serves. A CHANGELOG error is release-owned and amendable only by a dedicated docs PR, so it must be fixed before landing; harness: `scratchpad/pr-19934/harness/measure.ts` (corpus `metaTypes`) + `diff.mjs`.
- **B2 — wrong set in the changeset: "the four affected surfaces".** Measured affected producers, all description-only and eager-equal: the four named, plus `driverConfigJsonSchema` (+9, runtime-served), the react-blocks per-block conversion (+29; generated `.md` unchanged), and `reference-sites.ts`'s input conversion (+287). Either drop "the four affected" or enumerate; the qualitative sentence ("descriptions reappear. Nothing else does") is measured true on all of them.

Non-blocking:
- #19930 carried, unchanged by this PR: at head under `OS_EAGER_SCHEMAS=1` a first import of `src/api/index.ts`, `src/api/contract.zod.ts` or `src/data/index.ts` still throws "Cannot access 'FilterConditionSchema' before initialization"; `src/index.ts`, `src/shared/strict-object.ts`, `src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts`, `src/stack.zod.ts`, `src/automation/approval.zod.ts` load. The PR's child test enters through `kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts`, so it is not on the cycle.
- Dev's unfiled id-bearing note: answered above (P6a–d, pre-existing, 0 in corpus); a card only if a lazy schema ever takes an `id`.
- Dev's unfiled tsx env-hoisting note (`build-react-blocks-contract.ts:20`, `check-react-blocks-declaration-parity.ts:151`, `check-liveness.mts:167` believe they run eager): NOT MEASURED here, carried; after this PR their description parity no longer depends on the flag, so its stakes drop.
- Docblock wording (global registry by default; "lost" vs ancestor-emitted; snapshot semantics under in-place re-registration) — see ①.
- Suggested pins: a described `.strict().transform()` pipe, a Proxy referenced twice with both properties asserted, and one non-`description` meta key.

CI at the head, de-duplicated by name on latest `started_at`: 0 running, 0 failed. Success: Test Core (aggregate + 1/6–6/6), Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate (aggregate + 1/3–3/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Spec property liveness, filter, and the four claim guards. Skipped: Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in, not requested); Build Docs and Console Pin Gate (path filter, `filter` job in the same run); Auto Label and Check PR Size — their latest instances (the 01:02Z re-run after the body edit) skipped, the 00:57Z instances succeeded. The 8 checks running at spawn all completed green.
